$comment: Every place the app indexes a DECLARED collection by a literal integer. A hit is NOT automatically a defect — the sole-element and documented-last-resort forms are legitimate — but a NEW one must be argued for. Regenerate with `node scripts/lint-positional-declaration.mjs --write`; annotate in `notes`.

GUARDED — behind `arrays.length === 1` in the selection-union helper.
notes.libs/viz/src/viz-core/data/blendReduce.t: GUARDED — every hit sits behind `columns.length === 1` / `m === 1` (the single-column pass-through). Sole-element access, not a pick.
NOT a pick — `input.continuousColumns[0]?.length` reads a ROW COUNT, which every column of a frame shares. It is asking how many rows there are, not which column matters.
notes.libs/viz/src/viz-core/grid/useGridData.t: GUARDED (`catalog.layouts.length === 1 ? catalog.layouts[0].id : undefined`). A sole layout is not a choice; several refuse. Was an unguarded `layouts[0]` until this change.
notes.libs/viz/src/viz-core/heatmap-matrix/mat: OUT OF FAMILY — same pyramid convention, matrix side.
notes.libs/viz/src/viz-core/option/parse.ts|la: TWO hits, two different things. (1) `layouts.length === 1 ? layouts[0].id` is the SOLE-element access — not a choice at all, and the rule this whole change is built on. (2) `layouts[0]?.id` is a DOCUMENTED LAST RESORT: several layouts with no `encode.layout` declaration. It is a guess, and it is recorded rather than removed — two blind reviews established that refusing here blanks every multi-embedding dataset with no message and no recovery (there is no UI to choose a layout), which is the declare-and-MIGRATE shape a prior lifecycle already ruled on. What the change DID remove is the literal `'primary'`: a guess narrowed to the catalog's own declarations. Enumerated F11.
OUT OF FAMILY — multiscale PYRAMID indexing. `multiscales[0]`/`datasets[0]` is level 0, which is definitionally full resolution in the OME-Zarr spec, not a guess about which declaration was meant.
OUT OF FAMILY — same: pyramid level 0 is full-res by definition.
notes.server/src/modules/extensions/loader.rs|: in-source `#[cfg(test)]` assertions on a parsed manifest's first declared axis. Never ships.
notes.server/src/modules/extensions/types.rs|s: Both hits are #[cfg(test)] on a fixture that parses exactly ONE section (the first asserts c.sections.len() == 1 immediately above the index), so [0] is the sole-element form the rule permits — not an assumption about contributor-authored order. Recorded rather than silenced because this pair was invisible to the guard for the whole feature: the lint derives its field list from the GENERATED api types, and the openapi regen was deliberately deferred to fan-in so no partition would clobber it. The regen is what made `sections` a declared collection the guard can see. Any production read of contributes.sections must go by id.
notes.server/src/modules/workstore/data_api.rs: in-source `#[cfg(test)]` assertions pinning the ORDER the catalog reports axes in — asserting a position is exactly what a test of an ordering should do. Never ships.
notes.server/tests/extensions/api_test.rs|sect: Integration test over a fixture package declaring exactly one section; [0] is the sole-element form. A production read of contributes.sections must go by id.
notes.ui/src/core/workstore/artifactReader.ts|: SOLE ELEMENT: `previewableColumn` returns early unless `s.columns.length !== 1` is false, so `columns[0]` is the only element there is. The guard cannot see the guarding length check — that is what this note is for.
notes.ui/src/modules/datasets/components/Suppo: SOLE ELEMENT: `axes.length === 1 ? axes[0].name : ''` — the axis picker pre-selects only when there is nothing to pick.
notes.ui/src/modules/workbench/core/runtime/ax: 3 -> 4 with the coverage label the pane now renders instead of a repeated dataset name. `dims` is a declared SHAPE, whose ORDER IS THE DECLARATION (rows, then components) — the same licence already granted to `structure.axes`; it is not a contributor-authored collection whose order the contract leaves open. Every read is length-guarded and used only to compose a label, never to choose a candidate.
notes.ui/src/modules/workbench/core/runtime/re: Unit test asserting the registration seam over a single-section fixture; sole-element form.
notes.ui/src/modules/workbench/core/shell/Plac: `views[0]` as the default active tab of a placed area. `views` here is a RUNTIME pane list whose order IS the rendered tab order, not a contributor's declaration — the closest thing to a false positive in this ledger, kept because the field name is derived and narrowing the derivation by hand is how a guard stops guarding.
notes.ui/src/modules/workbench/extensions/canv: DECLARED DEFAULT, not a discovered candidate — `resolved.datasets[0].id` is the id the DECLARATION itself named first, and `<default>` is defined by canvasBinding's contract as 'whatever the declaration named its FIRST canvas.datasets entry'. Position 0 here is the author's own statement, in the author's own document.
REPORTED, not fixed this round — the `__canvasPanes` read-only e2e seam takes `option.datasets[0]` as the default dataset. Enumerated as F24 in .lifecycle/first-of-n-binding/FAMILY_ENUMERATION.md.

KNOWN, DELIBERATELY LEFT (DEC-13, and self-documented at the site). The project-wide `cat.layouts[0]` for a base that declares no `coords`. A prior lifecycle ruled this exact shape declare-and-MIGRATE, not declare-and-break, and named the blocker: one shipped analysis' scatter has no coordinate picker to declare from. Ending it here breaks a shipping surface; the remedy is a UI change to that analysis form.
notes.ui/src/modules/workbench/extensions/data: `ts.capabilities?.[0]` — the FIRST declared capability of a type selector, used as a display hint. A genuine positional read of a declared collection; it is a label, so a wrong pick mis-labels rather than mis-counts. Left recorded rather than fixed: this round's remit was the entity-axis class.

`makeFakeDataHost`'s synthetic column length. A FAKE plane whose caller seeds the axis list itself, so `axes[0]` is that fixture's own choice rather than an app semantic — but it is the same SHAPE, and it is recorded here so it stays visible if the fake is ever promoted.

MIXED, stated. 5 hits: (1) `axes.length === 1 ? axes[0].name` in `resolveEntityAxis` — the SOLE element, so no position is being privileged; (2) `declaredAxisOf`'s `structure.axes?.[0]` — `structure.axes` is positional BY STORAGE LAYOUT (`write_csc_zarr(axes=(row, col))`, row-major), which is the one place position genuinely means something; (3-5) `cat.axes[0]?.length` — the catalog's positional LAST RESORT, licensed by documented SILENCE only (a REFUSED ambiguous label never reaches it; see INV-3 in `resolveRowAxis`). The sixth — `rowAxisFor` resolving `Datatype.axes[0]` — is the leak this guard was built from and is GONE; planting it back is what proved the guard fires.
notes.ui/src/modules/workstore/project-extensi: NOT the contributed collection, and pre-existing: this `sections` is the array describeTypeSections() DERIVES inside the test from rows the test itself supplied — no contributor authors its order. It became a hit only because this guard keys on field NAME, so declaring `contributes.sections[]` in the generated api types retroactively captured an unrelated local of the same name. Counted here for honesty, not because the app indexes a declared collection at these lines.
notes.ui/src/modules/workbench/core/runtime/ax: SOLE-ELEMENT, and guarded as one. `soleDeclaredAxis` returns `axes[0]` ONLY when `axes.length === 1`; the plural case yields `undefined` rather than the first, because a multi-axis artifact (a matrix declares both) names no single axis and picking one is the `layouts[0]` guess. It reads the anchor key artifact's declared axis label, used in ONE direction only — a DIFFERENT label proves a different axis; an equal one proves nothing and falls through to the key-sequence digests.
notes.ui/src/modules/workbench/core/runtime/co: Sole-element form, guarded in the same expression: `datasets.length === 1 ? datasets[0] : null`. The fixture models a coordinate artifact whose source is either exactly one dataset or none — there is no Nth to take, and the guard is the condition, not a comment about it.
notes.ui/src/modules/workbench/core/runtime/pa: ITEM-8. GUARDED SOLE ELEMENT, not a positional read: the branch is taken only when `anchor.axes.length === 1`, so `[0]` is the whole collection rather than a position in it. The frame NAMES one row space (`row_space` / `row_space_label` / `row_space_length`), and an integrated coordinate resting on several has no one name and no one length — so the several-axes case deliberately yields `undefined` here and the labels read empty, rather than naming one of the pair. Taking `axes[0]` unguarded would be exactly the `layouts[0]` guess: a complete-looking name on a picture drawn from something wider.
